summary: VRSN, DPZ and CARG are the cleanest: top-of-sector gross profitability with operating cash flow well above net income, and 8 or 9 of 9 F-score tests passing. The menu is dated 2026-10-20, so its closes and some fiscal years are stale (WDFC, CLX, SBH, AAPL, TTEK), and several sector labels flatter the ranks (DPZ, MCO, MSCI, HWM). Lessons L1 and L2 apply to the proposer, news analyst and portfolio manager, not to me, and graded_calls is empty, so there is no track record to adjust for; I used news_memory only as context for the VRSN and TPR notes.

rankings.why: Only 9/9 F-score on the menu; gp_sector_pct 0.993, gross profitability 1.10; cfo $1.09B vs net income $826M on revenue $1.66B, so earnings are backed by cash. Newest 10-K of the top names (known_since 2026-02-05).
rankings.concerns: Net income is about 50% of revenue on a small asset base ($1.33B), so profitability is not cheap to defend. Menu close of 306.48 predates the 10-22 Q3 print (small EPS miss, revenue beat, guide raised per news_memory); that print is outside my fundamentals data.

rankings.concerns: Failed current_ratio_improved. Total assets of $662M against $907M revenue means the profitability ratio is sensitive to a small denominator.

rankings.concerns: Failed current_ratio_improved. News_memory shows two sell-side price-target cuts (UBS, Jefferies) ahead of the 11-05 print, which is sentiment, not accounting.

Labelled Materials (SIC nonferrous metals) but it is an aerospace components maker; sector percentile 0.859 is against the wrong peer set. FAST (Consumer Discretionary, industrial distributor), CART (Industrials) and LNG (SIC natural gas distribution, but an LNG exporter) have the same mismatch.
